findings.body: The docstring claims constant time, but the implementation calls sorted(), which is O(n log n). This contradicts the contract and will cause unexpected performance degradation on large inputs.

findings.anchor: query = f"SELECT id, status, total FROM orders WHERE customer_id = '{owner_id}'"
findings.body: The owner_id variable is interpolated directly into the SQL string using an f-string. This allows an attacker to inject arbitrary SQL commands if they control the owner_id input. Use parameterized queries provided by the database driver instead of string formatting.
findings.failure_scenario: An attacker supplies a malicious owner_id such as "' OR '1'='1"; the constructed query executes unintended SQL, potentially exposing or modifying database records.
findings.suggestion: query = "SELECT id, status, total FROM orders WHERE customer_id = %s"
findings.title: Parameterize SQL query to prevent injection

findings.body: The loop uses range(1, len(entries)), which starts at index 1 and skips the element at index 0. This means the first invoice entry is never scored or included in the ranking, causing incorrect results and potential data loss.
findings.failure_scenario: A caller passes a list of invoice entries. The entry at index 0 is ignored during scoring and sorting. The returned list is missing the first entry, leading to incomplete reports or downstream processing failures.
findings.title: Include the first element when iterating over entries

findings.anchor: def register_shipment_events(event_type: str, events: list[str] = []) -> dict[str, list[str]]:
findings.body: Using a mutable list [] as a default argument causes the list to be shared across all function calls that omit the events parameter. Subsequent calls will append to the same list, leading to unexpected state accumulation and data leakage between invocations.
findings.failure_scenario: A caller invokes register_shipment_events("type_a") without providing events. The default list is created and populated. A second caller invokes register_shipment_events("type_b") without events. The function appends to the same list, returning {"type_b": ["type_a", "type_b"]} instead of just ["type_b"].
findings.suggestion: def register_shipment_events(event_type: str, events: list[str] | None = None) -> dict[str, list[str]]:
findings.title: Replace mutable default argument with None
